<reason>Both sides were sharp and stayed on the motion as written, but PRO built the cleaner and more resilient path. PRO's two decisive levers survived: (1) CON's own "opt-in is a de facto ban" claim [B1.3], which PRO repeatedly converted into a concession that the practice depends on people not being asked, and (2) the twice-asked question of who speaks for the non-consenting third author (therapist, hotline, friend on another service). CON did answer the second question honestly — privilege, minimization, purpose limits, and the point that dual-party consent gives the third party no actual lever either — but PRO's reply that those are duties owed by others, enforced after the irreversible step by the same firm, was the more forceful comparison, and PRO's default-no rule at least prevents the taking. CON's best original move was the surplus/freeze dilemma over de-identification, which genuinely pressured PRO's scope; PRO absorbed it competently by embracing both horns ("if stripping works the motion is cheap; if it doesn't, names really are inseparable and you must ask"). CON's rebuttal of the "extraction" charge — that refusal is an artifact of alarming framing — was plausible but PRO turned it memorably in closing: a case that depends on how carefully you avoid saying "your messages to your doctor" is not a bargain anyone struck. The incumbency clash was roughly a wash. CON also carried an execution cost from a clipped opening. Net: PRO made the decisive clash easier to resolve and left its central confidentiality pillar unneutralized.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's handling of [B1.3] plus the third-party pressure question: by extracting that opt-in "would function as a ban," PRO reframed CON's efficiency case as dependent on non-disclosure, then combined it with CON's inability to give the therapist or hotline worker any pre-training lever. CON's counter — that a click is not voice and privilege/minimization already bind the firm — was the strongest reply in the debate but left the pre-emptive protection point standing.</best_rebuttal>
